correctness.rationale: For the counting-measure symmetric Laplacian and unit metric edges, gradients g_x=f(x)−f(o), z=−k⁻¹Σ_jg_j satisfy T=[[-2a,kb],[a,−(k+1)b]] and fast gradient deviations decay at b. The eigenvalues −α,−β give X(t)=[(β+d)e^(−αt)−(α+d)e^(−βt)]/Δ with d=kb−2a>0. Strict slow-edge domination follows from the exact fast-row absolute sum and the three-exponential comparison J(t)>0 (positivity/Jensen cases), not merely from numeric tests. An all-nonzero slow gradient row forces unique ± three-level ramps; the derivative X′ has one positive zero and the singular limit yields sup=2−1/(k+1), unattained when a>0. Independently exponentiated the full (k+2)×(k+2) Laplacian for four heterogeneous examples; the slow-edge norm matched the formula and strictly exceeded each fast edge.
